findings.claim: route fulfill executes attacker-chosen JavaScript in the page origin under deny:["eval"], reopening the exact mitigation security/page.mdx:20 documents
findings.evidence: Live raw-socket drive against a real Chrome: route **/pwned.html with an HTML body containing <script>document.title='ROUTE_EVAL_PWNED_JS_RAN'</script>, then navigate; title action returned ROUTE_EVAL_PWNED_JS_RAN while every one of evaluate/evalhandle/setcontent/addscript/addinitscript/removeinitscript/addstyle/expose/waitforfunction/cdp_url/inspect was denied by the same policy. route is in the network category only (policy.rs:186-198); body is arbitrary caller input (actions.rs:10071-10101).
findings.layer: runtime, raw daemon socket under an active --action-policy

findings.claim: adding inspect to DOCUMENTED_ACTIONS makes the pre-existing parity test launch a real browser and pop a DevTools window on every cargo test run, and makes it flaky
findings.evidence: parity_tests.rs:51 adds "inspect"; test_all_documented_actions_are_handled (parity_tests.rs:525) executes a minimal command per documented action; inspect is not in skip_launch_action so a browser is launched, then handle_inspect (actions.rs:4487) starts an InspectServer and calls open_url_in_browser (actions.rs:4508) which spawns `open http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. Observed directly: DevTools windows opened repeatedly during suite runs (user reported the devtools_app.html URL mid-review). Test failed 1 in 3 full-suite runs, 0 in 6 isolated runs.

findings.claim: the coverage test's source-text extractor misses any dispatch arm whose pattern is not a string literal, so a new uncategorized action can be added and the guard stays green
findings.evidence: Added `other if other == PWN_ACTION => handle_evaluate(cmd, state).await,` with `const PWN_ACTION: &str = "pwn_exec";` to execute_command. cargo fmt clean, compiles, test_policy_category_coverage_matches_dispatched_actions PASSES. The control (a plain `"pwn_exec" => ...` arm) correctly FAILS with "dispatched action 'pwn_exec' is missing from DOCUMENTED_ACTIONS". Also uncovered by construction: actions handled before the match (INTERNAL_DAEMON_SHUTDOWN_ACTION at actions.rs:2204 returns before the policy gate) and all sub-dispatch (find subactions, clipboard operation, dialog response).

findings.claim: auth_login fills two fields and clicks a submit button with only navigate appended, so deny:["fill"] and deny:["click"] do not stop credentials being driven into a page form
findings.evidence: handle_auth_login navigates at actions.rs:10508 then resolves username/password/submit selectors (10553 onward, auto_submit_selectors) and fills and clicks without re-entering the policy gate. policy_actions_for_command appends only navigate (actions.rs:2146). Mitigating: url comes from the stored profile, values come from the vault. Aggravating: usernameSelector, passwordSelector and submitSelector are caller-overridable per command.

findings.claim: MCP now accepts actionPolicy and confirmActions on every tool call, but the daemon only honours them at startup, so a per-call policy is silently ignored against a running daemon
findings.evidence: Started session rev2 with no policy; ran `--action-policy deny-all.json get text "#h"`; daemon pid unchanged (48290) and the command returned HELLO. mcp.rs:3585 appends the flags via append_common_global_args, shared by every tool. The daemon-startup-only consumption is at main.rs:1277.

findings.claim: docs/src/app/commands/page.mdx:585-586 still shows the pre-diff --action-policy help text while output.rs was updated
findings.evidence: grep of action-policy across the repo; commands/page.mdx mirrors the help block and reads "Path to action policy JSON file" / "Action categories requiring confirmation". AGENTS.md requires docs/src/app to be updated with output.rs.

findings.claim: vitals installs a persistent init script under deny:["eval"]
findings.evidence: handle_vitals calls mgr.add_script_to_evaluate(VITALS_INIT) at actions.rs:7316, the same primitive as addinitscript which is in the eval category; vitals is categorized get + navigate. Payload is a fixed agent-browser constant, not caller input, so no arbitrary execution, but the init script is never removed.

findings.claim: round 1: get grants arbitrary fills via find subactions
findings.evidence: Live: {"action":"getbylabel","subaction":"fill"} under deny:["fill"] returned "Action 'fill' denied by policy" before execution. policy_actions_for_command appends the subaction for every FIND_SUBACTION_COMMANDS entry except text (actions.rs:2133-2139). Under --confirm-actions the same path required two separate confirmations (getbylabel, then fill).

findings.claim: round 1: wait grants arbitrary JS via waitforfunction
findings.evidence: Live: waitforfunction denied by deny:["eval"]; the wait category now contains only wait, waitforurl, waitforloadstate, and plain wait still succeeded under the same policy.

findings.claim: round 2: deleting evalhandle/setcontent/addscript/addinitscript/addstyle/expose reopened arbitrary JS under deny eval
findings.evidence: All seven restored to the eval category and all seven denied live at the policy gate before execution; page title unchanged after the battery.

findings.claim: round 2: cdp_url parked uncategorized was a total policy escape
findings.evidence: Live: cdp_url and inspect both denied under deny:["eval"]; the gate fires before handle_inspect can start its server or spawn `open`.

Live: setvalue, clear, selectall, multiselect, inserttext, type, press, keyboard, keydown, input_keyboard, check, uncheck, select and clipboard write all denied under deny:["fill"]. dispatch is in click+interact rather than fill, and that is correct: dispatch_event (interaction.rs:831) only builds `new Event(type, init)` with both arguments JSON-escaped, so it cannot set a value or inject script. It is denied by deny:["click"], verified live.

exemptions.evidence: handler at actions.rs:5721 returns pid, socketDir, engine, launchHash and restore metadata including restoreLoadedPath and restoreSavedPath; it discloses local filesystem paths but no page content, no token and no CDP endpoint, and the daemon offers no file-read action to follow those paths with.
handle_pause (actions.rs:9004) returns a fixed json string and touches neither state nor browser; verified live, response was the static note only.

handle_confirm (actions.rs:10703) re-enters execute_command with the stored command, so deny rules run again; verified live that approving gettext did not approve innerhtml and that a find-fill needed two separate confirmations.
handle_deny (actions.rs:10723) takes the pending confirmation and returns; it has no execution path.

exemptions.claim: mcp.rs and output.rs edits are in scope
exemptions.evidence: AGENTS.md requires output.rs help, README, SKILL.md, docs/src/app and MCP parity to be updated in the same change as any user-facing flag change, so both files are mandated surfaces rather than scope creep, though R3-5 says the MCP exposure needs a guard.

exemptions.claim: responsebody in network rather than read is acceptable
exemptions.evidence: the diff documents response body under network in the new docs table, so the sharp edge (deny read+get+snapshot does not stop page content reaching the caller) is disclosed rather than hidden.

issue_candidates.title: {"default":"deny","allow":[]} fails open and permits every action
issue_candidates.evidence: policy.rs:327 guards the allow-list branch with !allow.is_empty(), and the else-branch that honours default:deny only runs when allow is absent. Verified live: a fresh daemon started with {"default":"deny","allow":[]} ran `get text "#h"` and returned HELLO.
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: the !allow.is_empty() guard is unchanged from origin/main; this diff only swapped the equality comparison inside it.

issue_candidates.title: __agent_browser_internal_shutdown bypasses the policy gate entirely
issue_candidates.evidence: actions.rs:2204 handles the internal shutdown action and returns before the policy block at actions.rs:2270, so a raw socket client can close the browser under deny:["state"] which contains close.
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: pre-existing ordering on main; denial of service only, no capability escalation.

issue_candidates.title: requests leaks full request headers under the network category
issue_candidates.evidence: live under deny:["read","get","snapshot","eval"], the requests action returned complete request header maps; on a real site that includes Cookie and Authorization.
issue_candidates.why_out_of_scope: correctly categorized as network by this diff; the gap is that the docs never state that a data-exfiltration posture requires denying network and state as well as read/get/snapshot.
